title: The first real evaluation pilot: what the notebook copilot and the agents actually do
request: Verify whether the R&D tools are correct in use, not only whether their tests pass: run the notebook copilot on real notebooks, call the live specialists, audit archived agent cycles and replay a trial.
spec: A frozen notebook suite (cells pinned by hash, expected signals and rationales) for the copilot on the HyperAck and churn notebooks; a live suite of five fixed specialist cases; an audit of archived Studio cycles and historical agent traces; a replay of one bank-marketing trial with the current worker. Every report is a new immutable file; no notebook is executed or edited and no holdout is used.
plan: Label seven notebook cases with expected findings and the rule that should be cited, pinning each cell's hash.
Run the copilot prototype on them and score detection and the retrieved proof.
Run the first of five live specialist cases against the configured provider.
Audit archived Studio cycles and 37 historical agent outputs against the current schema and contract checks.
Replay one fingerprinted bank trial with the current worker into a new folder and compare it byte for byte.

decisions.decision: Record a provider failure as a failed case, never replace it with a mock answer.
decisions.why: A synthetic response would turn an operational failure into a fake pass.

decisions.decision: Reject a changed notebook cell instead of re-scoring it against an old label.
decisions.why: The owner's notebooks evolve; a stale label silently scores different code.

decisions.decision: Do not train on the pilot's answers.
decisions.why: It would contaminate the cases that must later serve as an evaluation set.

change: dclab_rnd/notebook_eval.py with a frozen case manifest and dclab_rnd/agentic/live_eval.py (both later committed); the trace audit, the replay comparison and the system audit ran from tools that stayed on the author's machine (their tests skip until the files are committed); a pilot report, docs/REAL_EVALUATION_PILOT_2026-09-26.md.

findings.defect: The copilot missed a scaler and KMeans fitted on the full data before the split.
findings.scenario: The HyperAck notebook fits a scaler and KMeans on the full coordinate frame and adds geo_cluster before the later train/test split; the prototype's same-cell detector did not connect the fit to the split in another cell. It did catch full-data StandardScaler fitting before the split in other cells.
findings.cause: The prototype checked fits only within one cell.
findings.fix: Recorded as the pilot's next step 4 (fix the cross-cell pattern and keep the seven cases as development tests); the copilot rewritten on 2026-10-03 reviews notebooks in cell order with state carried across cells.
findings.test: The frozen case hyperack_full_data_clustering in the notebook suite.

findings.defect: A name-based leakage warning was worded as certain and cited the wrong rule.
findings.scenario: On the churn notebook the copilot called cancellation_date 'confirmed leaky' from its name alone, without the prediction moment or source timestamps, and cited DCLAB-R06 (score-gap interpretation) instead of DCLAB-R05 (a name is only a warning).
findings.cause: The warning text and the rule lookup did not distinguish a name match from a proven leak.
findings.fix: Recorded as a next step: word name matches as an availability question and cite DCLAB-R05; the owner must define churn's snapshot time and outcome horizon.
findings.test: The frozen case churn_cancellation_date_availability (wording 0 of 1, proof 3 of 4 overall).

findings.defect: The live planner could not be scored: the provider failed every attempt.
findings.scenario: The first specialist case was attempted three times on the configured model and once on another model name; every call returned InternalServerError with no response or token usage.
findings.cause: Provider-side failure; changing the model name did not restore access.
findings.fix: Recorded as failed cases, no further retries, and a provider-access check added to the owner worksheet before the suite is rerun.
findings.test: live_specialists probe reports kept as immutable files.

measurements.name: notebook copilot on fixed cases
measurements.gate: Development pilot on seven researcher-labelled cases; no accuracy threshold, and not a population estimate.
measurements.result: Detection 6 of 7; retrieved proof matched the predeclared rule 3 of 4; cautious wording 0 of 1.
measurements.next: Build a new, source-held-out, blinded notebook set with clean and flawed examples before claiming any accuracy.

measurements.name: archived Studio cycles and trial records
measurements.gate: Operational completion and an independent evidence audit of each trial record.
measurements.result: 3 of 6 cycles completed; 7 of 12 trial records passed the evidence audit; trace checks: 4 of 4 first proposals were transparent baselines, 26 of 26 citations referenced prior successful trials, 5 of 9 comparisons named a reference trial id, 1 of 37 outputs no longer validates against the current schema.
measurements.next: Remediate the five failing trial records; require an explicit reference trial id in every comparison.

measurements.name: bank trial replay with the current worker
measurements.gate: Metrics and out-of-fold predictions identical to the archived trial; a changed worker or catalog hash makes it a cross-version reproduction, not an exact replay.
measurements.result: ROC-AUC, AP, log loss and Brier identical (4 of 4); 4,000 out-of-fold records and the split fingerprint byte-identical; the exact-replay command refused because the worker and catalog hashes differ.
measurements.next: Label it a cross-version reproduction; it shows reproducibility, not validity on new data.

outcome: The first honest scorecard: the copilot is useful on a tiny development suite, the agents' decision quality is still unmeasured, and one trial reproduces exactly. Nothing here is proof of overall correctness; the release decision stayed false.
lessons: Passing software tests is not evidence that an agent decides well; measure behaviour on fixed cases and say how small the sample is.
Do not turn 6 of 7 on two notebooks into an accuracy claim.
A replay command that refuses when code hashes changed is a safeguard working, not a failure.
